#### ccf.products.constraints.resolve_effective_request

- Surface: ccf.products.constraints.resolve_effective_request
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `-> EffectiveRequest | ConstraintRefusal | PolicyResolutionConflict |
  ProductRequestViolation`; a refusal exit returned the refusal alone, and
  everything resolved before it — the defaults applied, the constraints folded,
  the pins consulted — was dropped on the floor
- After: `-> ResolutionOutcome`. Every one of the six exits constructs the
  outcome from the evidence accumulated at that exit: the conflict exit carries
  the defaults, the caller's values and every consulted pin; the
  required-absent exit the same, with no record for the absent key; the policy
  bound-refusal exit carries the bounds already attached to earlier keys; the
  technical bound-refusal exit carries the technical bounds attached so far;
  the validation exit carries the full effective set and the override attempts;
  the completion carries what `EffectiveRequest` was before, under
  `refusal=None`. `_with_overrides` still attaches the attempts to the refusal
  half, so a refusal reads as it did
- Why: `D-IMPL-264` D-07, Dave: *"Resolution participated whenever the
  resolution step actually ran. If it refuses halfway through, that partial
  work is still governed truth and belongs in replay."* A union that returned
  the refusal alone made that truth unrecordable by construction — the caller
  had nothing to record
- Migration: read `.refusal` for the determination (`None` when the resolution
  completed) and `.evidence` for the resolution. A call site that branched
  with `isinstance(resolved, (ConstraintRefusal, PolicyResolutionConflict,
  ProductRequestViolation))` becomes `if outcome.refusal is not None`; one
  that used the result as an `EffectiveRequest` reads `outcome.evidence`. The
  SDK's one call site (`GovernedResolver.resolve`) moved in this plan. The
  frozen cp-04 example's `assembler.py` keeps the old `isinstance` and is
  accepted evidence, not a compatibility requirement (`D-IMPL-264` am.1)

*Recorded by `24.7-02-resolution-returns-a-paired-outcome.md`.*

#### ccf.replay.record.build_replay_record

- Surface: ccf.replay.record.build_replay_record
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `resolution: "EffectiveRequest | None" = None`, last in the keyword
  list. `None` — the default, and what every caller that never thought about
  resolution passed — rendered dimension 2 as the sentinel
  `no-request-resolution`, so a decision whose resolution never ran and a
  decision whose caller dropped the resolution were the same artifact
- After: `resolution: "EffectiveRequest | ResolutionNotApplicable"`, keyword-
  only and REQUIRED, placed beside the other required inputs. Omitting it is
  a `TypeError` from the call itself; passing `None` is a `ValueError` naming
  *"an explicit resolution state"* and quoting P-2 — and that guard runs FIRST,
  before the outcome guards, because a missing resolution state is an
  integrity failure of the caller and not a malformed outcome; passing
  anything that is not an `EffectiveRequest` or a `ResolutionNotApplicable`
  (a pre-serialized string, for instance) is a `ValueError` saying the state
  is *"never accepted pre-serialized"*. Whichever value is passed is rendered
  once, from the value, through `canonical_bytes` — the `else` sentinel branch
  is gone
- Why: `D-IMPL-264` D-10, Dave: *"Make the builder require an explicit choice:
  effective/partial resolution, or a typed not-applicable marker with a
  reason. No implicit omission for new records."* And on the shape of the
  signature: *"The builder's signature should make omission impossible to
  express, not merely detected."* Sabotage executed: with the default
  restored, `test_the_builder_refuses_an_omitted_resolution` goes red because
  the omission is expressible again
- Migration: every caller passes `resolution=`. A caller whose path ran the
  constraint resolver passes the `EffectiveRequest` it produced (complete on
  the served path; on a refusal, the partial record the paired
  `ResolutionOutcome.evidence` carries — `24.7-02`). A caller whose path never
  invokes resolution passes
  `ResolutionNotApplicable(reason="no-resolution-step")`; a delivery boundary
  that refuses before resolution could begin passes
  `ResolutionNotApplicable(reason="refused-before-resolution")`. The 41 SDK
  test sites are re-derived in plans `24.7-04` (the 15 in
  `tests/replay/test_refusal_replay_record.py` and
  `tests/replay/test_dimension_extensions.py`) and `24.7-06` (the remaining
  26). The seven frozen example sites — cp-00, cp-01, cp-02, cp-03, s1-00 and
  s1-01 without `resolution=`; cp-04 with it — are NOT migrated: their reds
  are quarantined evidence under `D-IMPL-263` and `D-IMPL-261` (`D-IMPL-264`
  D-13, Dave: *"cp-00–cp-03 therefore become quarantined evidence if their
  existing calls fail under the new builder. Do not edit them."*)

*Recorded by `24.7-04-the-replay-builder-requires-an-explicit-resolution-state.md`.*

#### ccf.products.resolver.RefusalRecorderProtocol

- Surface: ccf.products.resolver.RefusalRecorderProtocol
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `record(..., resolution: EffectiveRequest | None = None)`. A caller
  could omit the keyword and the seam passed `None` to the builder, which
  wrote the sentinel — the omission the builder now refuses, delayed by one
  call frame
- After: `record(..., resolution: EffectiveRequest | ResolutionNotApplicable)`
  — keyword-only, NO default. The `@runtime_checkable` check still covers only
  the presence of `record`; `mypy` and
  `tests/products/test_resolver_seam.py::test_no_recorder_signature_defaults_the_resolution_state`
  (with a planted defaulting decoy as its control) read the signature. This
  reshaping is invisible to the generated manifest: the loop skips Protocols,
  which is why the fragment claims it here by name
- Why: `D-IMPL-264` amendment 1 (F-3 a), Dave: *"If the builder is fail-closed
  but the recorder still accepts `resolution=None`, then the API permits
  exactly the omission we are trying to prohibit and merely delays the failure
  by one call frame. Worse, having the recorder infer non-applicability would
  contradict Q10/Q13."* And the invariant, verbatim: *"Any API that constructs
  or delegates construction of a replay record must require an explicit
  resolution state: effective/partial resolution or explicit not-applicable
  marker. No intermediate layer may manufacture the marker from omission."*
- Migration: an out-of-tree recorder declares `resolution` keyword-only with
  no default and passes it through; every caller of any recorder passes it.
  cp-04's frozen `deployment.py:771` `recorder.record(...)` passes none and is
  accepted evidence under `D-IMPL-264` am.1, quarantined by `24.7-05`

*Recorded by `24.7-04-the-replay-builder-requires-an-explicit-resolution-state.md`.*

- Surface: ccf.products.resolver.build_governed_resolver
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: nineteen keyword arguments, seven optional
- After: twenty, eight optional. The new `product_gate: ProductGateProtocol | None = None` is threaded into both `GovernedResolver` constructions, and **both** halves of the declared-versus-supplied mismatch raise `TypeError` at build time: a class declaring a gate with no callable, and a callable against a class declaring none. Each message names the class key, the declared identity (or its absence) and the argument
- Why: a declared check that nothing executes is *"a default that nothing exercises*, which *is a check that stops checking without going red"* — an audit would read the declaration as an invariant in force. The mirror refusal exists because a deployment predicate running in the determination path with no declared identity gives `D-14` nothing to name
- Migration: none. `D-IMPL-282`'s *"no builder API break in 24.10"*: a class declaring no gate and a call naming none builds exactly what it built before, measured by `tests/products/test_resolver_defaults.py::test_a_class_declaring_no_gate_and_a_call_naming_none_is_unaffected`.

*Recorded by `24.10-02-the-declared-product-gate-runs-on-the-governed-path.md`.*

#### ccf.products.resolver.GovernedResolver

- Surface: ccf.products.resolver.GovernedResolver
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: seventeen constructor arguments, none with a default. Four arrived as manifest keys; the deployment's debt profile was not among them, so the class held the routing state and never the binding
- After: eighteen, still none with a default. The new `debt_profile_key: str | None` is the **fifth** manifest key, read off `BootedFabric.artifacts` like the other four rather than passed as an object — the class docstring's own rule, and the one that makes the profile served provably the one the manifest put in force. `None` is admissible and is the positive claim that this deployment declares no bands
- Why: `D-IMPL-117` — the populate half of the binding the SDK owes. Read by key rather than object because the resolved value travels inside the content address, and `obligation_for` forbids a Control Plane *"latest"* for the same reason (`D-IMPL-26`)
- Migration: every construction site must pass `debt_profile_key` (`None` where the deployment declares no profile), because this class is the auditable, defaultless composition. Callers reaching the fabric through `build_governed_resolver` are unaffected. Two sites in the tree moved: `tests/products/test_resolver_seam.py::_arguments` and `tests/products/test_evidence_derived_debt.py::_ask_the_empty_fabric`.

*Recorded by `24.11-03-the-resolver-carries-the-declared-obligation.md`.*

#### ccf.controlplane.artifacts.PolicyFilterParametersArtifact

- Surface: ccf.controlplane.artifacts.PolicyFilterParametersArtifact
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `permitted_classifications: frozenset[str]` — a literal envelope and nothing else
- After: `permitted_classifications: frozenset[str] | RequestBoundParameter`. A bare sequence is the literal variant and reads exactly as it always did; a mapping is the binding. **The two are variants of one field, so "a literal plus an independent binding" has no spelling** — which is what keeps an empty literal honest: `permitted_classifications: []` still means *admit nothing* and acquires no magical second reading (`D-IMPL-288`, Dave: *"Do not preserve the empty-list idiom by making it magical."*)
- Why: the artifact that owns the value declares how the value is obtained. Splitting one semantic value across two authority sites is the defect `24.11-02b` had just finished removing (`D-IMPL-292`)
- Migration: none for a literal declaration, and every shipped declaration is literal. Verified: a bare list still parses to the frozenset it always did.

*Recorded by `24.11-04-an-operator-parameter-may-be-request-bound.md`.*

#### ccf.assembly.worker.EntityResolutionRule

- Surface: ccf.assembly.worker.EntityResolutionRule
- Public surface: true

- Before: `entity_class`, `identity_keys`, `attribute_keys` — each declared identity key was read from the payload field of the same name, so a rule whose source names the value positionally (`parent_uri`, `child_uri`) put the field's name into the identity
- After: adds `identity_sources: Mapping[str, str]` — declared identity key → the payload field that supplies its value; defaulted to empty and hash-transparent, so a rule declaring nothing reads and hashes as it did. A remap of a key the rule does not declare as identity is refused at validation rather than ignored
- Why: `D-IMPL-316` (`592ade1b`) — this field changes where an identity value is read from; it does not change what constitutes identity. The declared key is still what is hashed

#### ccf_runtime.workflow.state.WorkflowStateRecord

- Surface: ccf_runtime.workflow.state.WorkflowStateRecord
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: six fields, the last being `workflow_definition_uri` — whose
  docstring said resume "validates the supplied handle against it, so an
  execution never continues under a definition it was not started with"
- After: a seventh required field, `workflow_definition_hash`, and the pair
  is what resume compares
- Why: the URI could not deliver what its own docstring claimed. The factory
  builds `definition_uri` from the artifact's declared `tenant`, `name` and
  `artifact_version` — never from the Control Plane key it was registered
  under — so a second definition registered under any other key carries a
  byte-identical URI while declaring different routing. Demonstrated: a
  substituted definition adding `credit-officer-approval -> elsewhere`
  completed there **with a genuine approver's action in hand**, spending a
  real human decision on a transition their workflow never declared
  (`SEC-001`, security review 2026-09-23)
- Migration: none for a caller. The engine writes the field; the record is
  the engine's own opaque state (D-IMPL-18/27) and no adopter constructs
  one. An execution suspended under an older record shape is not resumable
  across the change, which is correct rather than regrettable — the whole
  point is that the fabric can no longer be told what it was running

*Recorded by `350-01-a-gate-opens-on-a-human-action.md`.*

#### ccf.hitl.transport.HitlActionSubmission

- Surface: ccf.hitl.transport.HitlActionSubmission
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: six fields. A recorded submission said **what** a human did and
  **who** they were, and nothing about **which pending event** the action
  answered — so `WorkflowEngine._gate_authority` could not ask, and matched on
  `event_key` + tenant + product hash + `action in GATE_ACTIONS` alone.
  `GATE_ACTIONS` and `ESCALATION_ACTIONS` are the same two verdicts, so an
  action taken against an escalation that named the same event key satisfied
  an approval-gate check
- After: two optional fields, `answered_event_class` and
  `answered_workflow_state_ref`, **stamped by the transport and never by the
  submitter**. `submit` overwrites both from the event the transport itself
  observed being claimed through `remove`, and writes `None` when the
  submitter claimed nothing
- Why: a consumer of the authority path has to be able to ask "which
  primitive answered this, and about which execution?" and get an answer that
  the answerer did not author. Declared on the contract rather than kept in a
  transport side-table because the stamp has to travel with the action
  wherever the recorded submission travels
- Migration: none for a constructor — both fields default to `None` and any
  value a caller supplies is discarded at `submit` rather than rejected. A
  **third-party `HITLTransportProtocol` implementation must stamp**: one that
  does not leaves every submission reading `None`, and the engine's gate check
  then falls back to requiring the gate's own event to be still pending. That
  is fail-closed, which is the right direction, but it is a behavior change
  for such an implementation and it is why the obligation is written into the
  Protocol's `remove` and `submit` docstrings

*Recorded by `350-02-which-primitive-answered.md`.*

  `held_writable_class`. A refused write leaves the substrate byte-for-byte as it was

  and dialed out for any class
- After: a `governed=NOTHING_GOVERNED` keyword, a `governed` property, and
  `put(..., minted=None)` which runs `held_writable_class` **before the payload is
  encoded**, so a governed class never reaches the wire and the refusal is typed rather
  than whatever a remote server happened to answer — the posture `@latest` already had.
  The store behind the artifact server runs the identical check, so a remote client
  that skips this class and speaks to the server directly meets the same refusal

  re-deriving it

#### ccf_runtime.mcp.auth.TokenGrant

- After: adds `tenants: frozenset[str]`, carried into `AccessToken.claims`
- Why: `SEC-018`. A set rather than a scalar because the artifact store and HITL queue are deployment-wide surfaces one operator credential spans, and the only scalar encoding of that is a wildcard — a fail-open value the SDK would be holding on the deployment's behalf. **Empty means no tenant, never every tenant**, so a forgotten scope fails loudly. #### ccf_runtime.mcp.tenancy.TenantGuardedServer

- Surface: ccf_runtime.mcp.tenancy.TenantGuardedServer
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `TenantGuardedServer(server)`; `.tool(*, name, subject, mutating)` and `.resource(uri, *, subject, mutating)` guarded tenancy and called the body with the caller's arguments; `.fastmcp` exposed the raw server; `.untenanted()` was a fourth subject reading
- After: `TenantGuardedServer(server, *, authorizer: TenantAuthorizerProtocol)` — refused for a server already carrying a surface; `.tool(*, name, action, subject, resource, mutating)` and `.resource(uri, *, action, subject, resource, mutating)` decide the declared action on the declared resource and call `body(authorized, **wire_arguments)`; `.build()` replaces `.fastmcp` and raises on a smuggled surface; `.from_grant()` replaces `.untenanted()`; four resource readers (`resource_argument`, `resource_declared`, `resource_route`, `resource_composed`); `.ledger` maps names to `GuardedSurface`
- Why: `D-IMPL-353` §1.1 — the wrapper is the MCP mint site; a body must receive a capability for exactly its action or nothing, and a raw registration must be a boot failure rather than a test failure (§2 P9)

#### ccf.replay.record.ContentGenerationPath

- Surface: ccf.replay.record.ContentGenerationPath
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: sixteen members; the dimension related two instants — `request.asked_at`, carried on the request it holds, and the record's own `recorded_at`
- After: a seventeenth member, `served_at: datetime | None`, `Field(default=None, json_schema_extra={HASH_TRANSPARENT_KEY: True})` — **transparent at the sentinel**. A third instant, and the record now says all three rather than one of them twice: what the question asks as of, when the decision was taken, and when the answer was handed over. `recorded_at` is untouched on both the served and the refusal path
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` ruling 1. The mark is the ruling and not a preference: `None` — every record written before the member existed — canonicalizes exactly as it did, so no pre-1.0.2 address moves and the member's mere schema presence is not a generation boundary; a populated value participates, so **two serves of one question are two records**, which is the audit reading a bank needs. Deliberately NOT `ChildResolution.child_admitted_at`'s `{HASH_TRANSPARENT_KEY: False}`: the accepted design asserted transparency while citing that field as its precedent, and ruling 1 settles that this one is transparent. The precedent it actually follows is `ttl_anchor_at` on this same class — same shape, same sentinel, same mark
- Migration: none for a stored record. Every record written before the member existed rehydrates to the address it was written at, measured by the two rosters that hold the transparent set by name (`tests/contracts/test_hash_transparency.py` and `tests/replay/test_generation_mismatch.py`), both of which required this field to be DECLARED rather than merely marked. `THE_FIFTEEN` is unchanged, which is the load-bearing half: a row that grew that lineage would make an old record refuse. **For a caller that compares addresses across serves**: two serves of one question now differ, so any "same determination twice" assertion must pin the clock — which is what proves the clock is the only difference

*Recorded by `358-04-served-at.md`.*

#### ccf.replay.record.build_replay_record

- After: a new keyword-only parameter `served_at: datetime | None = None`, passed straight through to the dimension. Passed rather than derived, unlike the sibling `ttl_anchor_at` immediately above it in the same construction, which is read off the product because the product carries it — no artifact carries the instant the answer was handed over, so only the resolver that read the clock can supply it
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 4. One builder already mints every record on both the served and the refusal path, so the capture belongs in its signature rather than in a second construction
- Migration: none. The parameter defaults to `None`, so every existing caller writes a record whose address is exactly what it was

- After: twenty-eight — `temporal-bound-refusal` joins, and `_PRE_ASSEMBLY_REFUSALS` gains the type because the judgment is pre-acquisition and pre-graph-read, so no candidate exists and no lineage is invented for it. The token was checked against all twenty-seven for the vocabulary's substring rule (no token may contain another): no collision
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5. A refusal that is not in the roster cannot cross a door, be disclosed, or be given a status — the roster IS the vocabulary
- Migration: a consumer switching exhaustively on the kind gains one arm. Every structural gate over the vocabulary enumerated exactly what registration was owed and is green: the disclosure statement and minimal tables, the door's status map, the MCP parity check, and the per-kind envelope test

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.products.resolver.RefusalRecorderProtocol

- Surface: ccf.products.resolver.RefusalRecorderProtocol
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `record(...)` took `recorded_at` and no live instant, so a recorder had no way to state when a determination was actually made — and two of the five governed recorder families stamped live clock time into `recorded_at`, moving a refusal's dimension-1 boundary off the question
- After: a **required keyword** `served_at: datetime | None`, with no default and explicitly nullable. Required so no site can omit it; nullable so a surface that genuinely has no live instant asserts that rather than being assumed. The shape follows the ruling this module already quotes — `D-IMPL-264` amendment 1, *"No intermediate layer may manufacture the marker from omission."* `recorded_at` is untouched and is NOT a synonym: the question's instant bounds the record and the live instant travels beside it
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5. One invocation reads one clock, and every refusal it produces must carry that instant rather than a fresh one — a recorder that read its own clock would put two instants in one determination
- Migration: **every conforming recorder and every caller must pass it**, which the required keyword makes a type error rather than a silent default. All five governed families are migrated: the resolver's own path, `OpenedProduct`'s address refusal, the delivery boundary's four sites, the typed raised refusal, and the entitlement refusal. The most consequential repair is the address refusal, which had `request.asked_at` in scope three lines above and stamped `recorded_at=self._clock()` anyway

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.products.disclosure.EXTERNAL_STATEMENTS

- Surface: ccf.products.disclosure.EXTERNAL_STATEMENTS
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: no statement for the new kind, which the closure gate refuses
- After: one statement covering all three reasons, chosen so that it does not tell an external consumer a tenant is MISCONFIGURED — that is the operator's fact and exactly the internal state the minimal level exists to withhold. `PERMITTED_AT_MINIMAL` permits the two declared bounds and nothing else, on the `ttl-refusal` precedent: a declared ceiling is actionable, the fabric's own instants are not, and the policy key never crosses
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 with `D-IMPL-254` — what crosses a consumer boundary is the disclosure step's decision and no refusal type's
- Migration: none for existing kinds. At minimal, the undeclared reason discloses nothing actionable, correctly: nothing the caller could do would fix it

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.products.constraints.constraints_in_force

- Surface: ccf.products.constraints.constraints_in_force
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `constraints_in_force(control_plane, *, asked_at)` — the effectivity window was selected at the question's own instant
- After: `constraints_in_force(control_plane, *, served_at)`. A REQUIRED keyword with no default; the parameter is renamed rather than added beside, because its only job is the effectivity window and a retained `asked_at` would be an unused parameter inviting the two readings to diverge. `_require_aware` follows the instant — there is no implicit UTC in this fabric, and comparing a naive instant against an aware window answers for the wrong hour rather than raising
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 ruling B. A constraint that became effective after a question was asked but before it was answered now governs the answer, so a tenant that tightens a bound at noon has it in force at noon rather than from whenever the oldest in-flight question happened to be asked
- Migration: **every caller passes `served_at`, enforced as a type error rather than a silent default.** The superseded reasoning (`D-IMPL-253` Q6 — *"asked_at, absolutely. Otherwise replay of the same historical decision can resolve a different policy"*) is retained in the docstring because it names the risk that had to be answered before the instant could move; that risk is closed by a different mechanism, which is why the move is safe. Replay never re-derives effectivity: it resolves each binding at the version the record pinned, `ReplayResolver` has no `resolve_latest` to reach for, and nothing under `ccf/replay/` imports this module

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.products.constraints.applicable

- Surface: ccf.products.constraints.applicable
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `applicable(constraint, *, product_class, tenant, perspective_role, intent, asked_at)`
- After: the same four axes with `served_at` in place of `asked_at`. The four axes are unchanged; only the window reading moved, and the docstring now states which ruling amended which
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 ruling B. `applicable` and `constraints_in_force` share one `_in_window` reading precisely so the fabric cannot answer *"which policy was in force?"* two ways at two layers — so the instant had to move in both or in neither
- Migration: callers pass `served_at`. Measured: `applicable` has two executable callers and both are inside this module, so no external caller is affected

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.products.constraints.resolve_effective_request

- Surface: ccf.products.constraints.resolve_effective_request
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: no instant parameter — the function took `request` and re-checked applicability at `request.asked_at` on its own
- After: a REQUIRED keyword-only `served_at: datetime`. **This is the parameter whose absence would have made the whole change cosmetic.** The function independently RE-EVALUATES applicability, so a constraint set selected at `served_at` upstream would have been silently re-filtered at `request.asked_at` here — the selection undone with no error and no test red. A default would have let exactly that pass
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 ruling B, which names all three layers for this reason. The function stays pure: the instant arrives as an argument and no clock is read
- Migration: every caller passes `served_at`, including `ReferencePolicyConstraintResolver.resolve` and the `PolicyConstraintResolver` Protocol, which gain the same required keyword. A deployment substituting its own resolver conforms to the new signature or fails the Protocol check

#### ccf.controlplane.artifacts.DeploymentConfig

- Surface: ccf.controlplane.artifacts.DeploymentConfig
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: no way to declare a temporal boundary in configuration, so every config-driven deployment was undeclared under ruling 11 with no authoring surface to fix it
- After: an optional reserved section `temporal_boundary: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None`, marked `HASH_TRANSPARENT_KEY: True`. Transparent at its `None` sentinel, so **a config that omits the section keeps its pre-change content identity byte-for-byte** — measured on the existing reserved sections, which still derive exactly as before. Absence means *undeclared*; it does not mean unbounded and it synthesizes no policy. The body is the step-3 contract verbatim: no `semver` is injected, no tenant or key or registration metadata is accepted inside it, and the SDK supplies no duration default
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 section A. Ruling 11 admits no exception, so the declaration needs a home in the document an operator actually edits
- Migration: none required of an existing config — the field is optional and transparent at absence. A deployment that wants a bound adds the section; once enforcement lands (the remainder of step 5), a config-driven deployment without one will refuse

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.deployment.keys.DeploymentKeys

- Surface: ccf.deployment.keys.DeploymentKeys
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: no field naming the derived temporal-boundary key
- After: `temporal_boundary: str | None` — the canonical key the derivation minted, or `None` when the config declared no section. The key is always `temporal_boundary_policy_key(tenant_id=config.tenant_id)`; an author cannot override it, and stating `key`, `class_id`, `role` or `registration` inside the section is **refused by name** rather than ignored or honored. A section present with no top-level `tenant_id` is refused rather than keyed class-only or given an invented tenant
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 section A7. A caller that booted a deployment needs the address the policy was registered under without re-deriving it, and re-derivation at the call site is how two spellings of one key appear in one fabric
- Migration: additive; a reader that ignores the field is unaffected

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.products.composite.compose_children

- Surface: ccf.products.composite.compose_children
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `compose_children(..., ttl_anchor_at, decided_at, validity_floors)` — the mixing law measured each constituent's remaining validity from the DECISION instant
- After: the parameter is `evaluated_at` and the resolver supplies `served_at`. **The rename came with the value, deliberately:** a parameter named for one instant while carrying another is how the next reader re-derives the wrong one, and `D-IMPL-358` step 5 section I forbids leaving a variable named `decided_at` carrying `served_at`
- Why: how much validity a constituent has LEFT is a fact about the moment the answer is handed over, not about when the parent's question was decided. The function's own comment already said "a fact about now"; section I made "now" literal
- Migration: callers pass `evaluated_at`. Measured: one production caller (the resolver) and three in tests. The `D-IMPL-341` C11 control is migrated and **strengthened** — the fixture's three candidate instants are fifteen, ten and three minutes of remaining validity, so the new floor pair (four minutes refuses, two serves) separates all three readings where the old pair (twelve and nine) could only tell the evidence anchor from the decision

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.controlplane.artifacts.TtlBinding

- Surface: ccf.controlplane.artifacts.TtlBinding
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: each window was validated positive independently, and nothing compared them. A binding declaring `product_ttl_seconds` ABOVE its own `max_ttl_seconds` parsed cleanly — measured, it was accepted — and then failed Gate 3 on every single request as a governed `ttl-refusal`
- After: a model validator refuses that declaration at parse time. The boundary is INCLUSIVE (equal windows are admissible), matching Gate 3's own `expires_at <= now + MAX_TTL`
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 section H1. A binding that cannot ever serve is an operator's configuration error, and reporting it to the caller as a governed refusal on every question misattributes it to the party who cannot fix it — while nothing anywhere names the actual cause
- Migration: a deployment carrying such a binding now fails at boot instead of at every serve. It is **refused, never clamped**: silently lowering the product window would make the deployment serve under a TTL nobody declared — a value the fabric chose standing in for one the operator did not, which is the No-Hardcoding Rule's failure mode in miniature

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.client.adapters.inprocess.InProcessAdapter

- Surface: ccf.client.adapters.inprocess.InProcessAdapter
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `InProcessAdapter(address)` — a transport composed a governed resolver and took the fabric's clock implicitly, so two transports answering one question read two clocks
- After: `InProcessAdapter(address, *, clock=<the fabric's own clock>)`, threaded to the private `_boot` and on to `build_governed_resolver(admission_clock=…)`. **The injected fabric clock of `D-IMPL-159` / D6(d), not a test knob**: a transport IS a composition site, and this is where a composition states its now. The default is the fabric's own clock — imported from `ccf.products.resolver`, never restated, because a second definition would be a second clock — so nothing that does not care is affected
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5. `served_at` is read once per governed invocation and is non-sentinel, so it is inside the replay record's hash (`D-IMPL-243` amendment 1: *"Any non-sentinel value is rendered and must move the hash"*). Two serves at two wall times are therefore two record versions — which is the ruled identity rule, not a new one. The conformance parity legs compare `replay_ref` across transports and their contract has always been *"the same question at the same instant"*; the fixture never established the second half, and the wave made that visible. The transports agreed on the record's NAME and differed on its `@version`
- Migration: none required — the parameter is keyword-only and defaults to today's behavior. A composition that needs two transports to agree on a record version injects one clock into both. The boot cache memoizes per deployment root, so the first adapter to boot a root fixes that root's clock and a second naming the same root inherits it; that is `D-30`'s existing single-writer contract (one root is one fabric, and one fabric has one clock), not a new rule

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf.client.adapters.mcp_stdio.McpStdioAdapter

- Surface: ccf.client.adapters.mcp_stdio.McpStdioAdapter
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `McpStdioAdapter(address)`, resolving `as_of=None` with an ambient `datetime.now(UTC)`
- After: `McpStdioAdapter(address, *, clock=<the fabric's own clock>)`, and that clock is what resolves `as_of=None`. The same seam `InProcessAdapter` carries, with the same imported default — never a restated one
- Why: `D-IMPL-358` step 5 section H. The two adapters each resolved `as_of=None` client-side from an ambient clock. Once a composition can state its own now, an ambient read there pins `served_at` while leaving `asked_at` live — so the fabric would answer a question asked at one instant and serve it as of another. One clock per composition means one clock for both instants
- Migration: none required — keyword-only with today's behavior as its default. **The read stays CLIENT-SIDE:** relocating it to the door is the separate design question `C-13` recorded and declined, and this changes which clock it reads, not where. The clock does not cross to the child process either; a child composes its own, which is why the fixture deployment's program reads its instant from the environment

*Recorded by `358-05-trusted-time.md`.*

#### ccf_runtime.adapters.claude_agent.adapter.ClaudeAgentAdapter

- Surface: ccf_runtime.adapters.claude_agent.adapter.ClaudeAgentAdapter
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `ClaudeAgentAdapter(*, model, mcp_server_name, mcp_server_version, effects)`; `inject_context` put the joined system prompt on the carrier as a string, and the vendor's default transport spawned `claude` with the fabric's whole environment
- After: new keywords `child_environment: Mapping[str, str] | None = None` (`TP-02`), the complete environment, names and values, the child receives — `None` gives the child only `DEFAULT_CHILD_ENVIRONMENT`'s names (`PATH`, `HOME`) valued from the fabric; `cwd: str | Path | None = None`, the child's working directory, `None` meaning the per-call `0700` directory (`TP-02` options half, I-4); and `max_turns: int | None = None`, the turn budget, `None` meaning the vendor default (a budget, not a boundary). New members `transport(carrier)` (`TP-02`), `prompt_directories` and `remove_prompt_directories()` (`TP-05`). `inject_context` now writes the prompt to a `0600` file in a new `0700` directory and sets `system_prompt` to the vendor's typed file form; it sets the carrier's `env` to the allowlist, `tools=[]`, `setting_sources=[]`, `strict_mcp_config=True`, and `cli_path` to a path below `os.devnull` that can never exist, so the carrier fails closed on the vendor's default transport (I-3, `D-IMPL-361`)
- Why: `TP-02` — `ClaudeAgentOptions.env` merges over `os.environ` and cannot subtract, so every fabric secret reached the child; `TP-05` — a string `system_prompt` lands on the `claude` argv as `--system-prompt <text>`, readable by every local process and any process audit
- Migration: pass `transport=adapter.transport(carrier)` to `ClaudeSDKClient(...)` or `query(...)`; without it the vendor's default transport raises `CLIConnectionError` and starts nothing. Declare `child_environment` with every variable the CLI needs beyond `PATH` and `HOME` (an API key, a proxy). The CLI no longer loads host settings, built-in tools or foreign MCP servers; a deployment that relied on any of those must now provide them as governed skills. Declare `cwd` if the session needs a particular working directory, and `max_turns` if it needs a turn budget. Call `remove_prompt_directories()` once the sessions that used the carriers have ended.

*Recorded by `361-01-claude-adapter-and-stdio-door.md`.*

#### ccf_runtime.peering.typed_http.TypedHttpWire

- Surface: ccf_runtime.peering.typed_http.TypedHttpWire
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `(*, local_peer_id, endpoints, http_client, clock, receive_path, max_request_bytes)`. The receive queue was unbounded. The endpoint appended the inbound message and then minted the carriage identifier, so a payload that was not base64url was queued and answered `500`.
- After: adds `max_pending: int`, which is required, keyword-only, has no default, and must be positive (`ValueError` otherwise). The endpoint mints the carriage identifier first and answers `400` for a payload that cannot be named; such a payload is never queued. It then checks the bound immediately before the append. At the bound it answers `503`, with a plain-text body naming `ReceiveQueueFull`, and the queued messages stay intact and in order.
- Why: SEC-021 and Q13. A buffer size is a deployment's capacity decision, so the SDK ships no default (D-IMPL-38, D-IMPL-356).
- Migration: every constructor call must now pass `max_pending`. A sending peer sees the `503` as `PeerUnreachable` from `emit` and may retry once the receiver drains.

*Recorded by `369-21-sec-021-receive-queue-bound.md`.*

#### ccf_runtime.peering.lf_a2a.LfA2AWire

- Surface: ccf_runtime.peering.lf_a2a.LfA2AWire
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `(*, local_peer_id, agent_card, cards, http_client_factory, clock, rpc_path, max_message_bytes)`. The receive queue was unbounded.
- After: adds `max_pending: int`, which is required, keyword-only, has no default, and must be positive (`ValueError` otherwise). `_enqueue` checks the bound immediately before the append and raises `ReceiveQueueFull` at the bound. `a2a-sdk` returns that to the sending peer as a JSON-RPC error whose message begins `ReceiveQueueFull:`, and the queued messages stay intact and in order.
- Why: SEC-021 and Q13, as for `TypedHttpWire`.
- Migration: every constructor call must now pass `max_pending`. A sending peer sees the refusal as `PeerUnreachable` from `emit` / `emit_async`. Not covered here, and escalated separately: `a2a-sdk`'s JSON-RPC dispatcher reads the request body before this transport's checks run, so `max_message_bytes` bounds the carried envelope, not the bytes the process buffers.

*Recorded by `369-21-sec-021-receive-queue-bound.md`.*

#### ccf.products.child_resolver.GrantBoundChildResolver

- Surface: ccf.products.child_resolver.GrantBoundChildResolver
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: the legacy `CompositeChildResolverProtocol` call only; it handed each skill the deployment's `child_arguments` and never knew the subject the composite asked
- After: a new optional `child_questions: ChildQuestions | None` constructor argument and a `resolve_for(...)` method, so it now conforms to `RequestAwareChildResolverProtocol` and `GovernedResolver` hands it the composite's effective request. Each child's question is minted from that request through `child_questions`, and the child's answered subject is held to it. The legacy `__call__` remains and mints no question
- Why: a composite can only refuse a child that answered another subject if it knows the subject it asked, and that subject comes from the composite's request through the deployment's mapping — never from `child_arguments`, which is what the skill was handed
- Migration: supply `child_questions` (the same `ChildQuestions` mapping `QuestionBoundChildResolver` takes). Without it, or through the request-less `__call__`, every `local-dispatch` and `mcp` child is refused `question-mismatch` rather than admitted unbound. A wrapper that implements only `__call__` around this resolver must add `resolve_for` and delegate to it. Disclosed after the close panel (Fable, `D-IMPL-370`): `ChildArguments` carries no request or question, so the local-dispatch and `mcp` legs are now usable only by single-subject composites; a multi-subject composite's local or `mcp` child is refused `question-mismatch` (fails closed).

*Recorded by `370-25-sec-025-child-subject-binding.md`.*

#### ccf.graph.registry.BackendStore

- Surface: ccf.graph.registry.BackendStore
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: three members, `graph_identity`, `reader` and `close()`.
- After: a fourth, required member, `writer_lease() -> WriterLease`. Only the boot mint calls it, after the in-process check passes and before a token exists. It is never called at store open, because a read-only store over a live graph is legitimate. The SQLite reference store's lease is an exclusive `fcntl.flock` (never `lockf`) on `<resolved database path>.ccf-writer.lock`, opened with mode `0o600`. The Postgres reference store's lease is a session `pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtextextended(current_schema(), 0))`, never the blocking form. Both are `"cross-process"`. A store without the member is refused at boot by name, with a `TypeError`.
- Why: SEC-013. The single-writer guard was process-local, so two processes over one SQLite file or one Postgres schema each booted a writer.
- Migration: every out-of-tree adapter must add `writer_lease()` (see `public/how-to/write-a-graph-backend-adapter.md`). After this change, two processes that each boot one SQLite or Postgres deployment, such as two in-process client adapters or two MCP egress servers on one deployment root, exclude each other, and the second boot is refused. The `public/how-to/security-and-deployment.md` section on processes sharing a graph discloses the per-store scope, the local-filesystem requirement for SQLite, and the session-pooling requirement and silent lease loss on a dropped connection for Postgres.

*Recorded by `372-13-sec-013-writer-lease.md`.*

#### ccf.assembly.worker.EntityResolutionRule

- After: adds `attribute_authorities: Mapping[str, frozenset[str]]`, which maps a governed attribute to the `SourceIdentity.system_id` values allowed to assert it. It defaults to empty and is hash-transparent when empty (`D-IMPL-243`), so every existing rule keeps its content hash. An empty source set is fail-closed: no source may assert that attribute. A key that is not one of `attribute_keys` is refused at construction (`ValueError` naming `attribute_authorities`).

- Change type: reshaped
- Before: returned `RefusalReplayOutcome`.
- After: returns `RefusalReplayOutcome | ErasedReplayOutcome`. When nothing reads the children (the no-read path), an erased child is disclosed on the `RefusalReplayOutcome` and the reconstruction completes.
- Why: SEC-009; ruling 4.
- Migration: as for `replay`.

*Recorded by `374-04-sec-009-minimum-erasure.md`.*

#### ccf_runtime.mcp.artifact_server.build_artifact_server

- Surface: ccf_runtime.mcp.artifact_server.build_artifact_server
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `build_artifact_server(*, server_name, store, token_verifier, auth_settings, authorizer, entitlement_source, refusal_recorder, audit_log)`
- After: a new **required** keyword `control_plane: ErasureIndexSource`, with no default. The server wraps `store` through `compose_erasure_consult`.
  - Every byte read goes through the wrapped store.
  - A governed record follows the authorization-first order (ruling 1).
  - An erased artifact on the client lane is returned as the erased reading: the not-found shell at `minimal`, and `erased-content` above it.
  - The naming resource still resolves through `store`, because it returns an address, never bytes (the U8 reasoning).
- Why: SEC-009; the coordinator's MCP ruling on `D-IMPL-374` (4). This server is the ArtifactStore's persistence transport (CLAUDE.md §7.4), so an erased artifact served over it is exactly the SEC-009 hole.
- Migration: pass `control_plane=` with the deployment's `ControlPlaneRegistry`, the same registry the erasure door appends its mirror to. The five in-tree call sites are updated.

*Recorded by `374-04-sec-009-minimum-erasure.md`.*

#### ccf_runtime.authz.delivery_boundary.govern_dereference

- Surface: ccf_runtime.authz.delivery_boundary.govern_dereference
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: no erasure handling.
- After:
  - Authorization runs first: the principal and grant holds read the record through the unconsulted inner store. Those bytes are used only for the rights check and never leave the door.
  - Only then does the consulted read run. An erased address becomes the erased reading at the entitled caller's level.
  - A new keyword `erased_client_read: ErasedContentRefused | None = None` lets the MCP artifact server render an erased client-lane artifact the same way. It can only ever produce a refusal, never bytes.
- Why: SEC-009; rulings 1 and MCP on `D-IMPL-374` (4).
- Migration: none.

*Recorded by `374-04-sec-009-minimum-erasure.md`.*

#### ccf.replay.engine.ReplayOutcome

- Surface: ccf.replay.engine.ReplayOutcome
- Public surface: true
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: no erasure field.
- After: a new field `erased_content: tuple[ErasedContent, ...] = ()`. `RefusalReplayOutcome` gets the same field. It is hash-transparent at `()`, so an outcome with nothing erased renders as before.
- Why: SEC-009; design §5.2. A replay over erased retained content completes, and the erasure is disclosed on the result. The replay record is unchanged.
- Migration: none.

*Recorded by `374-04-sec-009-minimum-erasure.md`.*

#### tools/lints/__main__.py

- Surface: tools/lints/__main__.py
- Public surface: false
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `LINTED_TREES = ("src", "runtime", "examples")` and
  `RULE_TREE_SCOPE["no-hardcoding"] = ("src", "runtime", "examples")` — the
  No-Hardcoding Rule did not reach test modules
- After: both tuples gain `"tests"`. Two edits, not one: `run()` iterates
  `LINTED_TREES` and *then* filters each rule by `RULE_TREE_SCOPE`, so a tree
  named only in the scope map is never walked and the widening would be a
  no-op. `harness-imports`, `algorithmic`, and `orchestration-imports` stay
  `("src", "runtime")` — test modules exercising the harness adapters import
  harness SDKs, and CLAUDE.md §7.3 words that invariant over core
- Why: D-IMPL-78 (Dave, 2026-08-04). D-09 relocates the example CI assertions
  into `tests/`, and those assertions carry domain expectations read from
  `expected:` artifact blocks. Without this scope the relocation would move
  domain values out of a structural invariant's reach with every CI gate still
  green — a CI-invisible weakening arrived at as a side effect of an
  ergonomics change. The hole is closed before any relocation happens
- Migration: downstream forks that add test modules with inline domain
  literals — prompt-shaped strings, numeric threshold tables, direct `Agent` /
  `Task` / `Workflow` construction — will now see CI findings under
  `tests/`. The fix is the same one `/examples` already takes: read the
  expected value from the artifact the test asserts about, and construct
  agents through the Agent Factory from fixture artifacts. The exemption
  surface for a whole tree is this config file, never an allowlist entry

*Recorded by `15-04-lint-scope.md`.*

#### tools/lints/no_hardcoding.py

- Surface: tools/lints/no_hardcoding.py
- Public surface: false
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `cinv01a-prompt-shape` scored every prose-shaped literal that
  survived the SQL/URI/short-string filters. Developer-facing diagnostics were
  indistinguishable from prompts to the rule, so a multi-sentence CI failure
  message naming its own fix scored as a system instruction
- After: `is_developer_diagnostic()` runs before scoring. A literal that
  carries at least one `DIAGNOSTIC_MARKERS` signal — a backticked command, a
  repo-relative filename, a `callable()` reference — and does not
  `addresses_a_reader()` (role-preamble opener, second-person pronoun, or
  template-brace density) is a diagnostic, and is not scored
- Why: Dave's ruling of 2026-08-04, recorded in `15-03-audit-baseline.md` and
  binding on this plan: resolve the two prose-diagnostic false positives by
  refining the rule, **not** by adding allowlist entries. Two allowlist entries
  today becomes friction on every future diagnostic message, and this phase's
  conventions actively encourage diagnostics that name their own fix (15-01
  ships `test_the_drift_message_names_its_own_fix` asserting exactly that).
  The distinction is mechanically detectable: a prompt is a string sent to a
  model, a diagnostic is a string shown to a developer, and the old rule
  detected "long English string literal" — a proxy for the wrong thing
- Migration: a CINV-01a finding that was previously suppressed by an allowlist
  entry on a diagnostic message can have that entry deleted; none existed in
  this repo, and none were added. A genuine prompt is unaffected — the reader
  test means it cannot escape by mentioning a filename, proven by
  `test_a_prompt_wearing_diagnostic_markers_is_still_flagged`

*Recorded by `15-04-lint-scope.md`.*

#### src/ccf/controlplane/artifacts.py

- Public surface: false
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: the module docstring and the `DeclaredArtifact` class docstring both
  named "operator parameter sets" — unqualified — as a shape whose schema belongs
  to a deployment
- After: both say **deployment-authored** operator parameter sets, and both state
  the rule D-01 actually states: the SDK owns the schema of what it ships and
  never invents one for what it does not. The four categories the SDK ships have
  typed classes; everything else takes the open envelope
- Why: D-01. The unqualified claim was no longer true once this plan shipped the
  four typed classes, and amending only one of the two sites would leave the
  module contradicting itself. The policy-bundle rationale is kept intact — it
  was sound for policy bundles and remains the reason `DeclaredArtifact` exists;
  what changed is its scope, not its truth. mkdocstrings publishes both
  docstrings, so Phase 16's rendered reference changes with this edit, which is
  why it is a recorded surface change and not a comment tidy
- Migration: none — no name, signature or behavior changes; the docstrings are
  the deliverable

*Recorded by `15-08-operator-parameters.md`.*

#### ccf.signal-batch

- Surface: ccf.signal-batch
- Public surface: false
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: the event document used flat keys the SDK contract does not declare —
  `source_system_id:` for what the contract nests as `source: {system_id: ...}`,
  and `payload:` for what the contract calls `raw_payload:`. `tenant_id` was not
  in the event document at all; it was read from `ontology.yaml`
- After: the document is in the SDK's own envelope vocabulary — nested
  `source: {system_id: ...}` and `raw_payload:` — with `tenant_id` declared once
  on the batch, alongside the batch's `semver` lane
- Why: the translation between the two vocabularies is **removed rather than
  relocated**. The SDK does not grow a second field vocabulary for a shape it
  already owns, and D-15B permits the churn. The change is to the *container*
  keys only: `raw_payload`'s contents stay opaque to L1 and its keys stay the
  source system's vocabulary, exactly as `SignalEnvelope`'s docstring states
  (T-15-09-04, accepted). This entry is `Public surface: false` because an
  artifact-document format change can never appear in an `__all__`-derived
  manifest diff — see `docs/surface-changes/README.md`
- Migration: transform each event document mechanically —
  1. `source_system_id: X` becomes `source:` / `  system_id: X`
  2. `payload:` becomes `raw_payload:` (contents unchanged)
  3. add `tenant_id:` at the batch root, carrying the value previously read from
     the ontology document, and add `tenant_id:` on each envelope — the batch
     refuses a disagreement rather than stamping over one
  4. add the artifact's own `semver:` lane at the document root

*Recorded by `15-09-signal-perspective-productclass.md`.*

- Why: the catalog set is enumerated rather than globbed for the same reason the manifest is — the set of skills a deployment offers is governance. The document is `load` because a script for a run is not a statement of what the fabric may do; the grants it names become Control Plane state when the ledger accepts them, which is where the governance actually lives
- Migration: move the non-entry blocks of your skills bundle into a declared document and enumerate your catalog documents there

*Recorded by `15-14-examples-01-02.md`.*

#### examples/03-harness-portability/artifacts/product-class.yaml

- Surface: examples/03-harness-portability/artifacts/product-class.yaml
- Public surface: false
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: the `product_class:` block inside `controlplane.yaml`, with no declared operator set — `run.py` passed `operators.keys()` to the projection plan
- After: a `ccf.product-class` document carrying `max_ttl_key` and `required_operator_keys`, and deliberately no `max_ttl_version`
- Why: `required_operator_keys` is the authored declared side of Gate 2 (INV-CH7-47); a plan returning the registry's own keys made the gate compare a value against itself. `max_ttl_version` is minted by *registering* the ceiling, so an artifact declaring it would be authoring a hash of something it does not contain
- Migration: lift the block to the root, add `semver`, add `max_ttl_key` and `required_operator_keys`, drop `plan_id` and `product_ttl_seconds` (they moved to the governance document), and stop passing the registry's keys to your plan

#### ccf.graph._writer.mint_boot_token

- Surface: ccf.graph._writer.mint_boot_token
- Public surface: false
- Change type: reshaped
- Before: `mint_boot_token(*, graph_identity: str)`. It checked this process's live-writer table only.
- After: `mint_boot_token(*, store)`. It checks the live-writer table first, so the in-process refusal text is byte-identical to the old one. Then it acquires `store.writer_lease()`, records the lease beside the table, and records the lease scope on the token (`BootToken.lease_scope`). There is no parameter that skips the lease. `BaseGraphWriter.close` and `release_boot_token` drop the table entry first and then release the lease.
- Why: SEC-013. The lease is bound to the writer mint rather than to store open, and whether a lease applies is the store's declaration, never the caller's.
- Migration: none outside the SDK. The module is private, and `ccf.boot.boot` is its only caller.

*Recorded by `372-13-sec-013-writer-lease.md`.*

#### ccf.products.gates.effective_debt_ceiling

- Surface: ccf.products.gates.effective_debt_ceiling
- Public surface: true
- Change type: removed
- Before: `effective_debt_ceiling(*, declared: Decimal | None, requested: object)
  -> Decimal | None` — the class's declared ceiling folded with the request's
  `debt_tolerance` by `min`, returning a bare number
- After: gone. The fold is the Authority layer's now: the effective tolerance is
  resolved by `ccf.products.constraints.resolve_effective_request` and carried
  as an `EffectiveParameter` with the authority that set it and the pin it came
  from, never as a scalar. INTERIM, named in the source: the gate's debt half
  still holds a resolved tolerance to the class's ceiling as the floor of
  strictness — a request may tighten it and never loosen it — and `24.6-04`
  retires that half entirely
- Why: `C-06`; `D-IMPL-254` and `D-IMPL-253` Q1, Dave: *"We need to preserve
  provenance of authority. Otherwise we recreate exactly the defect the scout
  found with `min()`."* A bare number cannot say whether the ceiling in force is
  the class's or the caller's, and that is the whole question a refusal has to
  answer
- Migration: a deployment calling it directly reads
  `EffectiveRequest.parameter("debt_tolerance")`, which carries the value, the
  authority and the bound. Behavior at the gate is unchanged in this plan: an
  undeclared class is still unaffected whatever the request says, and a declared
  ceiling is still tightened and never loosened

*Recorded by `24.6-03-the-resolver-seam-effectivity-override-and-the-technical-capability.md`.*

  handler; the condition it named is now a construction-time refusal

## Behavior changes

Surfaces whose **signature did not move** but whose observable behavior did. A generated signature diff is structurally incapable of seeing these, which is why D-15 asks for a curated log alongside the manifest rather than instead of it.

252 entries — 220 public Python surface, 32 not public Python API.

### Public Python surface

#### ccf.hitl.transport.InMemoryHitlTransport

- Surface: ccf.hitl.transport.InMemoryHitlTransport
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `submit` verified the capability, the principal and (when required)
  the attestation, consumed the nonce, popped the claim and recorded
- After: `submit` snapshots the selected event under the lock, judges approver
  eligibility for approval-gate events when a Control Plane is bound (BEFORE
  attestation, G2 (a)), verifies the attestation, then under one lock
  revalidates the event (6a), consumes the nonce, pops the claim and records
  with the three new stamps. A submission refused at any step leaves
  `_submissions`, `_claims` and `_seen_nonces` unchanged
- Why: `D-IMPL-366` §4b, the RULED ordering
- Migration: none for admitted submissions; an ineligible approver, a
  wrong-class policy or a changed event is now refused

*Recorded by `006-approver-eligibility-is-the-sdks.md`.*

#### ccf.hitl.approval_gate.ApprovalGate

- Surface: ccf.hitl.approval_gate.ApprovalGate
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `resolve` verified the capability and the TOCTOU hash, then claimed
  and submitted
- After: with a Control Plane bound, `resolve` judges approver eligibility
  after the TOCTOU equality and BEFORE the atomic claim, raising
  `ApproverNotEligible` with the event still pending and `remove` never
  called
- Why: an ineligible resolution must not take the claim (`D-IMPL-366` §4 (4))
- Migration: callers of a bound gate handle `ApproverNotEligible` beside the
  signed-binding refusals

*Recorded by `006-approver-eligibility-is-the-sdks.md`.*

#### ccf.workflow.factory.WorkflowFactory

- Surface: ccf.workflow.factory.WorkflowFactory
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `construct` resolved each `gate_policies` target and checked the
  step kind, accepting any artifact class
- After: each `gate_policies` target must be a key the Control Plane binds to
  `ccf.approval-policy`, or construction is refused by name — every
  pre-change `DeclaredArtifact` approval policy included (§4 (5))
- Why: fail-closed at the factory for every gate that NAMES a policy, so a
  workflow whose named gate policy nothing can judge never constructs.
  **Disclosure (D-IMPL-366 close panel 3.2; ruled 2026-10-05):** a routed
  `hitl-gate` with NO `gate_policies` entry still constructs; its event
  carries `policy_ref=None`, and under a bound plane every approval of it is
  refused, so that gate can never be passed. Fail-closed at runtime, not at
  construction. A construction-time refusal of a policy-less routed gate is
  carried as a follow-on, not widened into this repair
- Migration: a typed policy is a NEW key and a NEW workflow definition
  version (D-IMPL-366 close panel 3.3; ruled 2026-10-05). A Control Plane
  key already bound to the pre-change `approval-policy` declared class cannot
  be rebound to `ccf.approval-policy` — `register_typed` refuses the rebind —
  so register the typed policy under a new key, publish a new definition
  version whose `gate_policies` pins it, and start executions under that
  version. Pre-change executions do not resume: their definition hash pins
  the old policy and their state record carries no starter (G5 (a)). The
  banking fixtures register their typed policies in a fresh plane
  (`tests/fixtures/banking/approval_policies.yaml`), which is why they can
  reuse the historical keys; a live deployment cannot

*Recorded by `006-approver-eligibility-is-the-sdks.md`.*

#### ccf_runtime.workflow.engine.WorkflowEngine

- Surface: ccf_runtime.workflow.engine.WorkflowEngine
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `execute` recorded no starter; `_gate_authority` admitted any
  recorded verdict naming the suspension, stamped or (while the gate was
  pending) unstamped
- After: `execute` stamps `started_by` from the `Execute` principal and every
  gate suspension carries it as `requested_by`; the authority predicate
  judges eligibility per submission against `gate_policies[gate]` and the
  record's starter, excludes `missing`-state submissions unconditionally, and
  admits an unstamped submission only when recorded against a pending event
  (or pre-change) while the gate is still pending. `SEC-001` conflict
  detection is unchanged: `_recorded_gate_verdicts` is not narrowed
- Why: the engine is the backstop for every path (`D-IMPL-366` §4 (4), §4c)
- Migration: a suspension persisted before this change refuses at resolution
  (G5 (a)); re-run it

*Recorded by `006-approver-eligibility-is-the-sdks.md`.*

#### ccf.deployment.operators.build_operator_registry

- Surface: ccf.deployment.operators.build_operator_registry
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `def build_operator_registry(*, parameters, view, pins, policy_bundle_key,
  similarity_index_version=None) -> OperatorRegistry` — the builder dispatched on artifact
  TYPE through an `isinstance` chain and raised `ValueError` on anything it did not
  recognise, so a deployment's own operator had no route into the registry the operator plan
  reads
- After: the same signature plus one defaulted, keyword-only parameter,
  `deployment_operators: Sequence[Operator] = ()`, whose members are registered FIRST and
  sorted by `operator.key`, through `register(operator)` with **no category argument**
- Why: `D-59`. The registry beneath the builder was already open —
  `src/ccf/operators/registry.py::OperatorRegistry.register` reads category and parameter
  schema off the operator — but the composition path in front of it was not, so
  `examples/cp-00-institutional-holders/deployment.py` had to register into a private
  registry the projection plan never sees. That workaround is exactly why cp-00's recipe
  witness for step 1 is `payload_key_present` rather than `operator_in_lineage`
- Migration: none — additive and keyword-only with a default

*Recorded by `24.1.1-02-the-deployment-operator-reaches-the-plan.md`.*

#### ccf.agents.assembler.DeterministicAssembler

- Surface: ccf.agents.assembler.DeterministicAssembler
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `(agent: 'Agent', projection: 'ProjectionOutput', acquisitions:
  'tuple[AcquiredContent, ...]' = ()) -> None` — the reference assembler could only succeed
  or raise, so the SDK's own worked example demonstrated *raise-or-succeed* while the
  codebase taught refusal-as-data
- After: the same constructor plus one optional field, `request_contract:
  'ProductRequestContract | None' = None`. With it absent the assembler is byte-for-byte
  what it was; with it present, `assemble` makes ONE call into
  `src/ccf/products/request.py::refuse_request` and RETURNS the resulting
  `ProductRequestViolation`
- Why: `D-IMPL-214`, ruling on criterion 6 — *"`DeterministicAssembler` is what deployments
  diff against. If only a test-local assembler can refuse, the reference impl still
  demonstrates 'raise or succeed' and criterion 6 becomes theater."* The conformity check is
  ordered AFTER the two identity checks, because a question asked of the wrong agent is not
  a question about a contract's conformity
- Migration: none — additive and keyword-only with a default

*Recorded by `24.1.1-03-a-refusal-returns-as-data.md`.*

#### ccf.contracts.canonical.canonical_bytes

- Surface: ccf.contracts.canonical.canonical_bytes
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: a `BaseModel` rendered every declared field
- After: a `BaseModel` renders every declared field EXCEPT a `True`-marked one whose value `==` its declared sentinel (compared by value, so a model-valued sentinel such as `NO_STORE_SNAPSHOT_PIN` compares by content). The same holds for `content_hash`, which hashes these bytes. Measured: eleven `content_hash` digests of the marked models at their sentinels are IDENTICAL to the `13bd250` tree's (`tests/contracts/test_hash_transparency.py`), CR-01's own pair now `34df2d94…` at both, and the directed twin `TraversalDescendantsParameters` — absent at base — hashing as the base three-field parameters did because the canonical form renders fields, never a class name; every non-sentinel value moves its hash
- Why: `D-IMPL-243` — "`_normalize` omits it when the value is that sentinel. Any non-sentinel value is rendered and must move the hash. That is not 'defaults never count.' It is 'silence equals yesterday.'"
- Migration: none for an adopter whose stores predate 24.5 on the marked models — their identities are what they were. `D-GATE-24.5` carries the sentence for everything else: adopter stores from before 24.5 are not promised byte-identical replay

*Recorded by `24.5-fix-01-hash-transparency.md`.*

#### ccf.replay.engine.replay

- Surface: ccf.replay.engine.replay
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: resolve the record byte-first, resolve bindings, plan, operators; re-execute; compare
- After: one step added between resolving the record and resolving its bindings, BEFORE anything is re-executed: the record's stored canonical object — obtained the way the record was resolved, a second `store.get` at the same address re-hashed to it (different bytes on the second read are `ReplayDivergence`) — is held against `generation_mismatch(DecisionReplayRecord, …)`, and a non-empty answer raises `ReplayGenerationMismatch` naming the fields. Signature unchanged; every record in the tree passes the step silently (measured: `tests/replay` 142 passed, 1 skipped, including the golden `13bd250` record and the pre-extension `PRE_CHANGE_CANONICAL`)
- Why: amendment 1 — "Declared scope + lint, at `replay()`. … Do not put this in `resolve_artifact`."
- Migration: none for any record in the tree or any record whose absent fields are `True`-marked or unmarked. A future field declared `False` makes every record written before it refused by name here — which is the declaration's meaning

*Recorded by `24.5-fix-01-hash-transparency.md`.*

#### ccf.products.request.refuse_request

- Surface: ccf.products.request.refuse_request
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: address → tier → payload; a `debt_tolerance` of `-1` under a `number` declaration conformed, reached `effective_debt_ceiling` as a "tightening" and refused every product `declared-obligation-refusal` with `declared="-1"`
- After: address → tier → payload → **tolerance interval** (`_refuse_tolerance`, module-private, last). The step reads `DEBT_TOLERANCE_PARAMETER` off `request.parameters` (a call-time import from `ccf.products.gates`, on the `DEF-17-02` pattern the payload import already uses); returns `None` when the key is absent, when the value is a `bool` or not an `int`/`Decimal` (those are the payload comparison's to name), or when the value is finite and `0 <= value <= 1`; otherwise `ProductRequestViolation(reason="not-a-proportion", key="debt_tolerance", declared_type=<the declared JSON type>, presented_type=<type name>, declared_keys=<arguments.properties>, presented_keys=<request.parameters>, detail="debt_tolerance: <value> is not a proportion — … [0, 1] … (24.5-L-14) …")`. Reads nothing about the class's ceiling: a request cannot create one, and a value that is not a proportion is not a tolerance under any class. Signature unchanged
- Why: WR-02. Last, for the converse of the reason the tier step is second: the interval step judges a number's magnitude, and only a declared, honored, well-typed number has one — so undeclared reads `undeclared-parameter`, declared-inert reads `not-supported-at-tier`, and a string `"-1"` under a `number` declaration reads `type-mismatch`, each exactly as before. Refusing at this boundary, rather than clamping at the gate, is what keeps `declared` on a `409` a number some class actually declared, and keeps `D-IMPL-224`'s one mechanism one
- Migration: none for a caller presenting a proportion. A caller presenting `-1`, `1.5`, `Infinity` or `NaN` now receives `product-request-violation` / `not-a-proportion` (no lineage; the graph is never touched) where it previously received a `declared-obligation-refusal` naming its own number as the class's — or, under a class declaring no ceiling, a served product

*Recorded by `24.5-fix-02-the-tolerance-interval-at-the-request-boundary.md`.*

#### ccf_runtime.http_api.routes.product.retrieve

- Surface: ccf_runtime.http_api.routes.product.retrieve
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: a `RefusalEnvelope` of kind `product-request-violation` fell through to `served_answer`, which raised `TypeError` — no response (an opaque 500 behind a real server)
- After: a second mapped kind beside the `409`: `envelope.kind == REFUSAL_KINDS[ProductRequestViolation]` → `JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={"kind", "refusal_type": "ProductRequestViolation", "refusal": <the whole envelope>})`, the `409`'s body shape. Mapped by KIND, so all six reasons of `ProductRequestViolationReason` (`undeclared-parameter`, `missing-required-parameter`, `type-mismatch`, `class-mismatch`, `not-supported-at-tier`, `not-a-proportion`) arrive as `400` through one branch; the envelope carries `reason`, `key`, both type names, both key sets, the request identity and `pre_assembly_lineage: null` (the verdict precedes the graph)
- Why: panel R3, Dave 2026-09-03. A request-conformity verdict is the caller's question failing the class's declared contract — the same family as the door's own request-shape refusals, which were already `400`; a `TypeError` for it was a door fault reported for a caller error
- Migration: none for a caller presenting a conformant request. A caller whose request is refused by the resolver's boundary now receives `400` with the envelope where it previously received a transport-level server error

*Recorded by `24.5-fix-03-the-http-door-answers-400-for-a-request-violation.md`.*

#### ccf.products.disclosure.INDISTINGUISHABLE\_BELOW\_FULL

- Surface: ccf.products.disclosure.INDISTINGUISHABLE_BELOW_FULL
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `{"subject-unavailable": frozenset({"detail", "cause",
  "error_code"})}` — three members, all of them either the envelope's `detail`
  or a key inside the refusal's `fields`
- After: the same entry with a fourth member, `policy_bindings`, which is a
  **whole member of the shell** rather than a `fields` key. `disclose` now
  normalizes such a member to the sentinel its own field declares — the empty
  tuple, which `RefusalEnvelope.policy_bindings` already documents as *nothing
  governed version-bearingly* — at every level below `full`
- Why: an entitlement denial pinned the entitlement policy that decided it, at
  its version, and an assembler's nonexistent-subject determination pinned
  nothing. So the two D-27 subjects differed by **value** and — because the
  canonical rendering omits an empty tuple — by **key presence** too, which is
  the *body schema/field presence* channel `D-IMPL-253` amendment 2 (4) names
  by name. `24.6-08` F-2 flagged it, `24.6-09` F-1 and `24.6-10` F-1 measured
  it at each door, and `D-IMPL-258` (2) ruled it closed at the disclosure step
  rather than allowlisted in the tests
- Migration: **a refused consumer no longer learns which Control Plane policy
  governed a `subject-unavailable` refusal, at `minimal` or `reasoned`.** A
  client reading `refusal["policy_bindings"]` on that kind finds the key absent
  below `full`; a deployment that wants the pin back sets its tenant's
  `ProductEntitlementPolicy.disclosure_level` to `full`, which is a versioned
  Control Plane statement that this reader may see internal truth. Nothing an
  examiner reads moves: the internal envelope on the Decision Replay record
  still carries the real bindings, and both door controls assert it

*Recorded by `24.6-D-IMPL-258-the-disclosed-shell-normalizes-its-policy-bindings.md`.*

#### ccf.products.disclosure.INDISTINGUISHABLE\_BELOW\_FULL

- Surface: ccf.products.disclosure.INDISTINGUISHABLE_BELOW_FULL
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `{"subject-unavailable": frozenset({"detail", "cause", "error_code",
  "policy_bindings"})}`. A delivery-boundary denial carried the
  `ResourceRequestIdentity` it was decided against (`D-IMPL-256` (1)) on the
  disclosed shell at every level, and an assembler's nonexistent-subject
  determination carried none, so the key's PRESENCE told the two subjects
  apart below `full`. The phase's own equivalence instruments excluded the
  member on Dave's *"request identity … may legitimately differ"* rider; the
  close review measured the channel and `D-IMPL-260` P-J ruled it closed
- After: the same entry with a fifth member, `resource`. Below `full`,
  `disclose` normalizes it to the member's own sentinel — `None`,
  hash-transparent — so neither shell renders the key; the
  `DisclosureDecision` records `resource` among what was withheld. At `full`
  it crosses whole. The internal envelope on the Decision Replay record keeps
  it at every level. Both equivalence instruments now compare the member
  (value and presence) instead of excluding it
- Why: `D-IMPL-260` P-J, and `D-IMPL-253` amendment 2 (4) by name: *body
  schema/field presence* is a channel, and one member's presence was carrying
  the whole distinction. Excluding it from the instrument would have been the
  allowlist `D-IMPL-258` (2) refused for `policy_bindings`
- Migration: **a refused consumer no longer learns what resource, on which
  surface, at what instant a `subject-unavailable` denial was decided against,
  at `minimal` or `reasoned`.** A client reading `refusal["resource"]` finds
  the key absent below `full`; the `replay_reference` still resolves, and the
  record's internal envelope carries the identity for the examiner. A
  deployment that wants it on the wire sets its tenant's
  `ProductEntitlementPolicy.disclosure_level` to `full`. Tests that read the
  identity off the shell now read it off the record

*Recorded by `24.6-D-IMPL-260-the-bound-carries-its-reason-and-crosses-without-its-provenance.md`.*

#### ccf.products.door.door\_refusal

- Surface: ccf.products.door.door_refusal
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: `door_refusal(resolved, *, asked, identity=None, product_class,
  version) -> RefusalEnvelope | None`. Two refusal shapes crossed: a
  `RefusalEnvelope` passed through untouched whatever its `replay_reference`
  or `disclosure` said, and a BARE refusal value — any type `REFUSAL_KINDS`
  names — which the door enveloped itself, supplying the question from
  `asked` or from the `identity` a question-less surface stated. That envelope
  was undisclosed and unrecorded: a determination reaching a consumer with no
  replay and no disclosure decision behind it, released by the layer
  `D-IMPL-254` says decides nothing. The close review measured it as P-A
- After: `door_refusal(resolved) -> RefusalEnvelope | None`. Only a
  `RefusalEnvelope` that PROVES its governance crosses — `replay_reference`
  other than `NO_REPLAY_REFERENCE` and `disclosure` not `None`, which is
  exactly what `ReplayRefusalRecorder.record` returns. A bare refusal value,
  an envelope at the sentinel, or an envelope with `disclosure=None` raises
  `UngovernedResolverResult`; a served shape returns `None` as before. The
  four keyword arguments are gone with the translation they fed
- Why: `D-IMPL-260` P-A, verbatim: *"the boundary must accept only a
  typed/provable governed result proving determination, replay and
  disclosure completed; a nonconforming resolver result must not cross"*
- Migration: **a deployment resolver that returned what `run_gates` gave it
  must now record it.** Hand the bare value to the SDK's
  `ReplayRefusalRecorder.record` (the seam `build_governed_resolver` wires,
  and the one every door is built with) and return the envelope it hands
  back; a question-less surface's request identity is what that seam records.
  Callers of `door_refusal` drop `asked`, `identity`, `product_class` and
  `version`. A resolver still returning a bare value reaches its callers as
  the door's opaque runtime failure, never as a refusal

*Recorded by `24.6-D-IMPL-260-the-bound-carries-its-reason-and-crosses-without-its-provenance.md`.*

#### ccf.products.door.served\_answer

- Surface: ccf.products.door.served_answer
- Public surface: true
- Change type: behavior
- Before: accepted `ServedProduct` and the narrower `ServableProduct`, reporting
  `ServedAnswer(replay_ref=None)` for the second — `D-IMPL-148` Addendum A's
  *"named divergence"* — so a gate-admitted vessel nothing had recorded was
  served with no replay behind it
- After: accepts `ServedProduct` only; `ServedAnswer.replay_ref` is `str`, never
  `None`. A bare `ServableProduct` raises `UngovernedResolverResult` with a
  message naming the fix (`ccf.replay.serve.serve`); any other shape raises the
